Base directory for this skill: /Users/michaelrihm/Documents/Projects/toolkit-v2/plugins/work/skills/work-decide

# Work decide

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Walks the owner through what waits on him, one decision at a time, and records each answer where it belongs. Track these steps with the host's plan tool (Claude Code: the task list; Codex: `update_plan`), not in the reply.

## Steps

1. Build the queue. The command lists each decision once: requirements waiting for approval, proposed designs, results at stage 11, Open Questions rows the owner decides, and memory proposals. Its "Agent to-do" lines are not decisions. A delivery offer belongs to `work-delegate`: open it after his other decisions.
   `toolkit work decisions`
2. He gave an answer without being asked ("approved", "go with B"): match it to exactly one waiting decision; when two could match, ask which, naming both. A bare "yes", "ok", or "looks good" with no question asked is not an answer (`references/approvals.md`, section 1).
3. Otherwise start with the count and one short line for every waiting decision, memory proposals included ("3 decisions wait on you: the WI-004 design, the WI-006 result, and a memory proposal about deploy days."). Then take them one at a time, the one blocking the most work first: what is decided, the choices, your recommendation and its main reason, and what happens after each answer. One decision per message, in the reply text.
4. An approval: read the item, then run that gate's checklist in `references/approvals.md` (requirements: section 2; design: section 3; result: section 4).
   `toolkit work show <id>`
5. An Open Questions answer: save his words first, rewrite that row with the answer, the date, and Answered, then set `waiting_on` back (`references/recording-owner-answers.md`, sections 4 and 5).
   `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect '<what the answer changes>'`
   `toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Open Questions' --set-file <file>`
   `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
6. A memory proposal: show its one line and your recommendation. Yes: approve it. No: reject it, and never propose the same fact again (`references/proposals.md`).
   `toolkit memory approve <key> --by <owner>`
   `toolkit memory reject <key>`
7. A decision for the whole project: add the row inside the `publish-docs` save workspace, in the order in `references/decisions-log.md`.
   `toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner>`
8. A "no" or a change: record it as the answer, move the item back (for example to refinement), and open the skill that redoes the work.
   `toolkit work set <id> --stage 02-refinement`
9. Lead with "Not saved" if any write failed. Update the current focus when an answer changed an item's next step (`references/current-focus.md`). After each recorded answer, list the decisions again and name what still waits on him, memory proposals included, by name ("One decision still waits: the memory proposal about Ghost slugs."). A decision an earlier reply said you would take next is taken next. Empty queue: say so and offer `work-on` for unblocked items. End with the next decision's question or the exact words that continue.
   `toolkit work decisions`

## Gotchas

- Run each `toolkit` command alone: never joined by `&&`, `;`, or a pipe, and never from a script (in Codex that runs it inside the sandbox, where it fails). One-line values go in single quotes, never double quotes; an apostrophe inside them is `'\''` in Claude Code and ’ (U+2019) in Codex, or reword the text. Section text goes on standard input (`--set-file -`) in Claude Code, and in `--text '<text>'` or a `mktemp -d` file in Codex (`references/toolkit-commands.md`, "Text in a command").
- Every decision carries a recommendation, even when it is the only one in the queue. A bare question is not enough.
- Ask in the reply text, never through a question tool.
- The approve command marks the Open Questions rows that asked for it Answered and prints "Marked Q-xx Answered". Never edit those rows again by hand.
- `waiting_on`: `agent` when the agent continues, `none` when nothing waits, `owner` while another of his questions on that item is still open. The approve command sets `none` by itself.
- A memory proposal is not a fact until he approves it. Do not rely on it.
- An approval never covers merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.
- After a result approval, the item continues with `work-finish`. Open it when he wants it shipped now.
- GitHub Issues or Jira: `toolkit work` exits with code 3. Build the queue from the labels in `references/tracker-github.md` or `references/tracker-jira.md`, and remove the waiting-on-owner label after each approval or last answer.

## Example decision message

```markdown
WI-015 needs your choice of design.

- Option A: use the built-in report page. Ready in about a day; the layout is fixed.
- Option B: a custom page. About a week; any layout you want.

I recommend A, because every requirement is met without custom code.
After A: I plan the build. After B: I plan a longer build and ask you about the layout.

Do you approve Option A?
```

## References

| File | Open it when |
| --- | --- |
| [references/approvals.md](references/approvals.md) | Step 4: the checklist for each gate; step 2: what counts as an answer |
| [references/decisions-log.md](references/decisions-log.md) | Step 7: a project-wide decision, `DECISIONS.md`, replacing a decision |
| [references/proposals.md](references/proposals.md) | Step 6: a memory proposal |
| [references/recording-owner-answers.md](references/recording-owner-answers.md) | Step 5: where an answer goes, history notes, `waiting_on`, a failed save |
| [references/work-item-format.md](references/work-item-format.md) | Before rewriting a section or an Open Questions row |
| [references/current-focus.md](references/current-focus.md) | Step 9: an answer changed an item's next step |
| [references/toolkit-commands.md](references/toolkit-commands.md) | Before a command that carries text, and on any exit code other than 0 |
| [references/tracker-local.md](references/tracker-local.md) | `tracker.type` is `local` |
| [references/tracker-notion.md](references/tracker-notion.md) | `tracker.type` is `notion` |
| [references/tracker-github.md](references/tracker-github.md) | A `toolkit work` command exits 3 in a GitHub Issues project |
| [references/tracker-jira.md](references/tracker-jira.md) | A `toolkit work` command exits 3 in a Jira project |

1	<!-- Generated file. Source: plugins/work/shared/approvals.md. Edit the source, then run node dev/tools/sync-skill-references.mjs. -->
2	# Approvals and gates
3	
4	The exact steps to ask for and record each owner approval, and what counts as
5	one. Run each checklist in order; one wrong or missing command leaves the
6	item in the wrong state.
7	
8	## Contents
9	
10	1. What counts as approval
11	2. Requirements approval
12	3. Design approval
13	4. Result approval
14	5. Done
15	6. Cancel
16	7. Delivery offer
17	8. Project-wide decision
18	9. Memory proposal
19	10. Sub-items and approvals
20	11. Standing merge instruction
21	12. When an approve command refuses
22	
23	## 1. What counts as approval
24	
25	`toolkit work lifecycle` prints the gates and these rules. In short:
26	
27	- Only the owner's explicit words count. Quote them in a history note.
28	- A question, a suggestion, a tentative answer ("probably B"), silence, or a
29	  saved draft is not approval.
30	- An approval covers only what was shown. It never covers merge, deployment,
31	  spending, or publishing.
32	- An approval survives later stages. A stage alone does not prove approval:
33	  check the approval field (`toolkit work show <id>`).
34	- A bare "yes", "ok", or "looks good" answers only a yes-or-no question asked
35	  earlier in this conversation. When none was asked, or the waiting question
36	  is not a yes-or-no question, show the decision with its choices and your
37	  recommendation, and record nothing.
38	- After a yes, save his words first, in a history note that starts with
39	  `Owner said:`. Then run the gate's commands. A command that refuses then
40	  never loses his answer, and no later session asks him again.
41	- `--by <owner>` is his name exactly as `toolkit config get project.owner`
42	  prints it (for example "Mike Rihm", not "Mike"), so every approval names
43	  him the same way.
44	- When an approve command notes that the item's Overview still asks for
45	  that approval (Next action), write the step after the approval with the
46	  `toolkit work edit` command the note prints.
47	
48	| The owner says | After this question | It is |
49	| --- | --- | --- |
50	| "Yes, approved." | "Do you approve these requirements?" | The requirements approval |
51	| "Go with B." | The design options with a recommendation | The choice and approval of Option B |
52	| "Looks good." | "Do you approve this result?" | The result approval |
53	| "Looks good." | "Shall I split WI-12 into these three sub-items?" | A yes to the split only, not a result approval |
54	| "ok" | Nothing was asked in this chat | Not an answer; ask what he wants |
55	| "Probably A, but let me think." | The design options | Not an answer; the design stays proposed |
56	| "Ship it." | He has seen the result, gaps, and evidence | The result approval (record it with his words) |
57	
58	## 2. Requirements approval
59	
60	Asked by `work-requirements`. `work-decide` records a later answer.
61	
62	Before asking:
63	
64	- [ ] The Agreed goal holds real text. The CLI refuses the approval while it
65	      still holds the template text.
66	- [ ] The spec check ran (`requirements-analyst`), and its findings were fixed
67	      or turned into questions.
68	- [ ] No Open Questions row linked to a requirement is still open. If one is,
69	      say which and ask it first.
70	
71	Ask: show the Agreed goal, each requirement in one line, the Acceptance list,
72	and any open question. Then ask exactly "Do you approve these requirements?"
73	as the last line, and set the item waiting on the owner.
74	
75	```text
76	toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on owner
77	```
78	
79	After his yes, in this order:
80	
81	- [ ] Save his words first, so no later session asks him again.
82	      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Requirements approved.'`
83	- [ ] Set each approved `R-xx` Status to Finalized and add who approved it and
84	      when to its Decision record, in one edit of `Active requirements`.
85	      `toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Active requirements' --set-file <file>`
86	- [ ] Record the approval. It adds its own history row, marks the Open
87	      Questions rows that asked for it Answered, sets `waiting_on` to `none`,
88	      and moves an earlier item to stage 03.
89	      `toolkit work approve <id> --requirements --by <owner>`
90	- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent, unless another question for him is
91	      still open on it.
92	      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
93	- [ ] Check the record.
94	      `toolkit work validate <id>`
95	- [ ] Next: a `build` or `data-load` item goes to `solution-design`, unless the
96	      owner agreed to skip the design. Say a skip in the final reply, not in a
97	      progress line.
98	
99	Not yet, or a change: the item stays waiting on him. Record the change and
100	ask again.
101	
102	A yes that arrives later (`work-decide` records it):
103	
104	- The Agreed goal still holds the template text: write the goal he was shown
105	  with the approval question, then record the approval.
106	  `toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Agreed goal' --text '<goal he was shown>'`
107	- A requirement still has a linked open question: say which one, open
108	  `work-requirements` for it, and record the approval once it is answered,
109	  without asking him again.
110	
111	## 3. Design approval
112	
113	Asked by `solution-design`. `work-decide` records a later answer.
114	
115	Before asking:
116	
117	- [ ] The design is saved as proposed, and the item waits on the owner. Add no
118	      Open Questions row for the design approval itself: a proposed design is
119	      already listed as his decision.
120	      `toolkit work design <id> --set-file <file> --status proposed`
121	      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on owner`
122	
123	Ask: the options in one sentence each, your recommendation and its reason,
124	what he will see when it is done, the main risks, and the build order. Then
125	ask him to choose or approve.
126	
127	After his yes, or his choice of one option, in this order:
128	
129	- [ ] Save his words first, so no later session asks him again.
130	      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Design approved; work-on plans the build.'`
131	- [ ] Fill "Recommendation and owner decision": Owner decision (who, when,
132	      where he said it) and Reason for decision (his reason only; never invent
133	      one).
134	- [ ] Fill every "Selected design" subsection and the "Build and verification
135	      plan" (Technical sequence, and Acceptance checks with one row per
136	      requirement). `work-check` reads those checks.
137	- [ ] Remove every leftover template prompt. Leave the Design status line as
138	      it is.
139	- [ ] Save the design text.
140	      `toolkit work design <id> --set-file <file>`
141	- [ ] Record the approval. It adds its own history row. It refuses (exit
142	      code 2, `design_not_filled`) while "Selected design" still says
143	      "Pending owner decision" or holds the template prompt: save the filled
144	      design first, then run it again, without asking him again.
145	      `toolkit work approve <id> --design --by <owner>`
146	- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent, unless another question is still open.
147	      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
148	- [ ] Check the record.
149	      `toolkit work validate <id>`
150	
151	He wants changes: record them in the design's Notes > Design changes during
152	the interview, run a fix round for the named changes only, save it as
153	proposed again, and ask again.
154	
155	## 4. Result approval
156	
157	Asked by `work-check` at stage 11.
158	
159	Before asking:
160	
161	- [ ] The tests and every acceptance check ran, and an independent checker
162	      reported, or you say plainly that no independent check ran.
163	- [ ] The check is recorded in a history note (what was checked, the
164	      evidence, the gaps).
165	- [ ] The item is at stage 11 and waits on the owner. Add no Open Questions
166	      row: stage 11 already lists the result as his decision.
167	      `toolkit work set <id> --stage 11-user-approval --waiting-on owner`
168	
169	Ask: what it does now in his terms, how he can see it himself, the evidence,
170	and the gaps. Then ask exactly "Do you approve this result?" Never hide a gap
171	to get a yes.
172	
173	After his yes, in this order:
174	
175	- [ ] Save his words first.
176	      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Result approved; work-finish continues.'`
177	- [ ] Record the approval.
178	      `toolkit work approve <id> --result --by <owner>`
179	- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent.
180	      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
181	- [ ] Open `work-finish`.
182	
183	A "no": record his words, turn each problem he names into a task or a
184	requirement change, and continue checking.
185	
186	## 5. Done
187	
188	Asked by `work-finish`. Only `toolkit work finish` sets Done.
189	
190	Before the finish command:
191	
192	- [ ] The result approval is recorded, or you have the owner's own words
193	      approving this result to pass with `--quote`.
194	- [ ] Every change the item made is committed and reached the default branch,
195	      or the owner said to leave it on the branch.
196	- [ ] Requirements and system guide updates are saved through `publish-docs`.
197	- [ ] Every open sub-item is finished, cancelled, or moved, or the owner said
198	      the parent is done anyway.
199	- [ ] Every Roadmap phase the item completed says Done.
200	- [ ] Overview: Related items current, Current position "Done on <date>:
201	      <evidence>", Blockers "None.".
202	- [ ] Leftover worktrees and branches for the item are listed and offered for
203	      removal.
204	
205	Then run one of these:
206	
207	```text
208	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>'
209	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --quote '<his exact words>'
210	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --allow-open-sub-items
211	```
212	
213	The second is only for a result approval not yet recorded. The third is only
214	for a parent the owner said is done while sub-items are still open; quote his
215	words in a history note. The command sets Next action and Resume here, and
216	prints what still needs a note.
217	
218	The finish command also backs up `.work-items/` and `.memory/` (and Hindsight
219	memory) to the owner's backup folder and prints one line about it. Read that
220	line:
221	
222	- "Backed up ... to <folder>": done. Say it in one line in the reply.
223	- "No backup folder is set ...": ask the owner for a folder outside the
224	  project, as a question in the reply. After his answer:
225	  `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or `none` when he wants no backup).
226	- A line with "failed" or "Tell the owner": tell him that line as it is. The
227	  item is still Done; only the backup is missing.
228	
229	## 6. Cancel
230	
231	Asked by `work-finish`. Only `toolkit work cancel` sets Cancelled.
232	
233	- [ ] The reason is the owner's own words, not a summary.
234	- [ ] Each open sub-item: ask whether to cancel it, move it to the top level,
235	      or move it under another item. Never cancel them without asking.

# Approvals and gates

The exact steps to ask for and record each owner approval, and what counts as
one. Run each checklist in order; one wrong or missing command leaves the
item in the wrong state.

## Contents

1. What counts as approval
2. Requirements approval
3. Design approval
4. Result approval
5. Done
6. Cancel
7. Delivery offer
8. Project-wide decision
9. Memory proposal
10. Sub-items and approvals
11. Standing merge instruction
12. When an approve command refuses

## 1. What counts as approval

`toolkit work lifecycle` prints the gates and these rules. In short:

- Only the owner's explicit words count. Quote them in a history note.
- A question, a suggestion, a tentative answer ("probably B"), silence, or a
  saved draft is not approval.
- An approval covers only what was shown. It never covers merge, deployment,
  spending, or publishing.
- An approval survives later stages. A stage alone does not prove approval:
  check the approval field (`toolkit work show <id>`).
- A bare "yes", "ok", or "looks good" answers only a yes-or-no question asked
  earlier in this conversation. When none was asked, or the waiting question
  is not a yes-or-no question, show the decision with its choices and your
  recommendation, and record nothing.
- After a yes, save his words first, in a history note that starts with
  `Owner said:`. Then run the gate's commands. A command that refuses then
  never loses his answer, and no later session asks him again.
- `--by <owner>` is his name exactly as `toolkit config get project.owner`
  prints it (for example "Mike Rihm", not "Mike"), so every approval names
  him the same way.
- When an approve command notes that the item's Overview still asks for
  that approval (Next action), write the step after the approval with the
  `toolkit work edit` command the note prints.

| The owner says | After this question | It is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Yes, approved." | "Do you approve these requirements?" | The requirements approval |
| "Go with B." | The design options with a recommendation | The choice and approval of Option B |
| "Looks good." | "Do you approve this result?" | The result approval |
| "Looks good." | "Shall I split WI-12 into these three sub-items?" | A yes to the split only, not a result approval |
| "ok" | Nothing was asked in this chat | Not an answer; ask what he wants |
| "Probably A, but let me think." | The design options | Not an answer; the design stays proposed |
| "Ship it." | He has seen the result, gaps, and evidence | The result approval (record it with his words) |

## 2. Requirements approval

Asked by `work-requirements`. `work-decide` records a later answer.

Before asking:

- [ ] The Agreed goal holds real text. The CLI refuses the approval while it
      still holds the template text.
- [ ] The spec check ran (`requirements-analyst`), and its findings were fixed
      or turned into questions.
- [ ] No Open Questions row linked to a requirement is still open. If one is,
      say which and ask it first.

Ask: show the Agreed goal, each requirement in one line, the Acceptance list,
and any open question. Then ask exactly "Do you approve these requirements?"
as the last line, and set the item waiting on the owner.

```text
toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on owner
```

After his yes, in this order:

- [ ] Save his words first, so no later session asks him again.
      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Requirements approved.'`
- [ ] Set each approved `R-xx` Status to Finalized and add who approved it and
      when to its Decision record, in one edit of `Active requirements`.
      `toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Active requirements' --set-file <file>`
- [ ] Record the approval. It adds its own history row, marks the Open
      Questions rows that asked for it Answered, sets `waiting_on` to `none`,
      and moves an earlier item to stage 03.
      `toolkit work approve <id> --requirements --by <owner>`
- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent, unless another question for him is
      still open on it.
      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
- [ ] Check the record.
      `toolkit work validate <id>`
- [ ] Next: a `build` or `data-load` item goes to `solution-design`, unless the
      owner agreed to skip the design. Say a skip in the final reply, not in a
      progress line.

Not yet, or a change: the item stays waiting on him. Record the change and
ask again.

A yes that arrives later (`work-decide` records it):

- The Agreed goal still holds the template text: write the goal he was shown
  with the approval question, then record the approval.
  `toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Agreed goal' --text '<goal he was shown>'`
- A requirement still has a linked open question: say which one, open
  `work-requirements` for it, and record the approval once it is answered,
  without asking him again.

## 3. Design approval

Asked by `solution-design`. `work-decide` records a later answer.

Before asking:

- [ ] The design is saved as proposed, and the item waits on the owner. Add no
      Open Questions row for the design approval itself: a proposed design is
      already listed as his decision.
      `toolkit work design <id> --set-file <file> --status proposed`
      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on owner`

Ask: the options in one sentence each, your recommendation and its reason,
what he will see when it is done, the main risks, and the build order. Then
ask him to choose or approve.

After his yes, or his choice of one option, in this order:

- [ ] Save his words first, so no later session asks him again.
      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Design approved; work-on plans the build.'`
- [ ] Fill "Recommendation and owner decision": Owner decision (who, when,
      where he said it) and Reason for decision (his reason only; never invent
      one).
- [ ] Fill every "Selected design" subsection and the "Build and verification
      plan" (Technical sequence, and Acceptance checks with one row per
      requirement). `work-check` reads those checks.
- [ ] Remove every leftover template prompt. Leave the Design status line as
      it is.
- [ ] Save the design text.
      `toolkit work design <id> --set-file <file>`
- [ ] Record the approval. It adds its own history row. It refuses (exit
      code 2, `design_not_filled`) while "Selected design" still says
      "Pending owner decision" or holds the template prompt: save the filled
      design first, then run it again, without asking him again.
      `toolkit work approve <id> --design --by <owner>`
- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent, unless another question is still open.
      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
- [ ] Check the record.
      `toolkit work validate <id>`

He wants changes: record them in the design's Notes > Design changes during
the interview, run a fix round for the named changes only, save it as
proposed again, and ask again.

## 4. Result approval

Asked by `work-check` at stage 11.

Before asking:

- [ ] The tests and every acceptance check ran, and an independent checker
      reported, or you say plainly that no independent check ran.
- [ ] The check is recorded in a history note (what was checked, the
      evidence, the gaps).
- [ ] The item is at stage 11 and waits on the owner. Add no Open Questions
      row: stage 11 already lists the result as his decision.
      `toolkit work set <id> --stage 11-user-approval --waiting-on owner`

Ask: what it does now in his terms, how he can see it himself, the evidence,
and the gaps. Then ask exactly "Do you approve this result?" Never hide a gap
to get a yes.

After his yes, in this order:

- [ ] Save his words first.
      `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Result approved; work-finish continues.'`
- [ ] Record the approval.
      `toolkit work approve <id> --result --by <owner>`
- [ ] Hand the item back to the agent.
      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent`
- [ ] Open `work-finish`.

A "no": record his words, turn each problem he names into a task or a
requirement change, and continue checking.

## 5. Done

Asked by `work-finish`. Only `toolkit work finish` sets Done.

Before the finish command:

- [ ] The result approval is recorded, or you have the owner's own words
      approving this result to pass with `--quote`.
- [ ] Every change the item made is committed and reached the default branch,
      or the owner said to leave it on the branch.
- [ ] Requirements and system guide updates are saved through `publish-docs`.
- [ ] Every open sub-item is finished, cancelled, or moved, or the owner said
      the parent is done anyway.
- [ ] Every Roadmap phase the item completed says Done.
- [ ] Overview: Related items current, Current position "Done on <date>:
      <evidence>", Blockers "None.".
- [ ] Leftover worktrees and branches for the item are listed and offered for
      removal.

Then run one of these:

```text
toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>'
toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --quote '<his exact words>'
toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --allow-open-sub-items
```

The second is only for a result approval not yet recorded. The third is only
for a parent the owner said is done while sub-items are still open; quote his
words in a history note. The command sets Next action and Resume here, and
prints what still needs a note.

The finish command also backs up `.work-items/` and `.memory/` (and Hindsight
memory) to the owner's backup folder and prints one line about it. Read that
line:

- "Backed up ... to <folder>": done. Say it in one line in the reply.
- "No backup folder is set ...": ask the owner for a folder outside the
  project, as a question in the reply. After his answer:
  `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or `none` when he wants no backup).
- A line with "failed" or "Tell the owner": tell him that line as it is. The
  item is still Done; only the backup is missing.

## 6. Cancel

Asked by `work-finish`. Only `toolkit work cancel` sets Cancelled.

- [ ] The reason is the owner's own words, not a summary.
- [ ] Each open sub-item: ask whether to cancel it, move it to the top level,
      or move it under another item. Never cancel them without asking.
- [ ] `toolkit work cancel <id> --reason '<his words>'`

Cancelling keeps the record. Nothing is deleted.

## 7. Delivery offer

Only `work-delegate` makes the offer and records the answer. Every other skill
opens `work-delegate` for it. The recorded value:

```text
toolkit work set <id> --delivery agent-led
toolkit work set <id> --delivery owner-led
```

A delivery answer never approves requirements, a design, or a result, and
never widens merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.

## 8. Project-wide decision

Recorded by `work-decide` as a row in `DECISIONS.md` at the project root,
then committed through `publish-docs`.

```text
toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner>
toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner> --replaces D-<n>
```

`DECISIONS.md` is append-only. A changed decision is a new row that names the
one it replaces. Any skill that meets a project-wide decision opens
`work-decide`, which runs the full order of work with `publish-docs`.

## 9. Memory proposal

A memory the owner did not answer ("Save to memory?") is saved as a proposal:
status `needs-review`. The agent does not rely on it until he approves it.

```text
toolkit memory approve <key> --by <owner>
toolkit memory reject <key>
```

A rejection deletes the proposal. Never propose the same fact again in other
words.

## 10. Sub-items and approvals

- A child made with `--covers R-02,R-03` links those parent requirements and
  inherits the parent's requirements approval. The owner is never asked to
  approve the same requirement twice.
- A parent design the owner approved covers its `--covers` children: they
  start at planning (stage 06) with no design of their own.
- A child that needs new behavior gets its own `R-xx` and its own approval.
- Each sub-item needs its own result approval. The owner's approval of the
  parent does not cover it.
- Finishing a sub-item never finishes or approves its parent.

## 11. Standing merge instruction

A merge normally needs the owner's yes to that merge. A standing merge
instruction replaces that yes only when all of these hold:

- [ ] `DECISIONS.md` records it as the owner's decision (the project's
      `AGENTS.md` may point at it);
- [ ] an `acceptance-checker` that did not build the change reported no
      blocking issue on that exact head commit;
- [ ] every check passes on that head;
- [ ] the work item does not say its merge needs the owner's approval (an
      item that says so overrides the instruction).

Without an independent check the instruction does not apply: ask the owner.
A new commit after the check means a new check on the new head.

## 12. When an approve command refuses

- Show the owner the command's error in plain words. Never work around it by
  editing the record, the design text, or a header field.
- The error names what is missing (for example the Agreed goal still holds
  the template text). Fix that, then run the same command again.
- Exit code 2 means a refused gate: the record is unchanged.

# Work finish

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Takes an approved item through the pull request, merge, deployment, and requirements update to Done, or cancels it; it never marks Done without the owner's approval and never runs a production deploy. Track these steps with the host's plan tool (Claude Code: the task list; Codex: `update_plan`), not in the reply.

## Steps

1. Check the result approval is recorded. Not recorded: show the result, the gaps, and the evidence, and ask. "Ship it" or "mark it done" after he saw the result counts: save his words first, then record it (`references/approvals.md`, section 4). Each sub-item needs its own.
   `toolkit work show <id>`
   `toolkit work history <id> --note 'Owner said: <quote>' --effect 'Result approved; work-finish continues.'`
   `toolkit work approve <id> --result --by <owner>`
2. Repository work: commit the item's files by name on its branch, push it, open the pull request, and set the stage (`references/closing.md`, section 2; `references/git-rules.md` before any Git write).
   `toolkit work set <id> --stage 12-pr-and-push`
3. Merge through `merge-and-clean-up` only with the owner's yes to this merge, or a standing merge instruction with an independent check on the exact head (`references/closing.md`, section 3). No remote: the local merge (`references/closing.md`, section 4), then this note.
   `toolkit work history <id> --note 'No remote: merged locally into <default branch>.' --effect 'No pull request; no deployment.'`
4. Deployment, when the item needs one (`references/closing.md`, section 5). Production deploys and production data loads are the owner's to run. Salesforce: a sandbox validate runs; a sandbox deploy needs his yes for that deploy, and in Codex he runs every sandbox deploy and sandbox data change himself, so give him the exact command with its `-o <sandbox>`. Run each `sf` command directly, never from a script.
   `toolkit work set <id> --stage 13-deployment`
5. Requirements baseline: copy only delivered and approved behavior into the area's file in `requirements/`, update `system-guide/` when the structure changed, and save both with `publish-docs` (`references/closing.md`, section 6).
   `toolkit work set <id> --stage 14-spec-update`
6. Sub-items: list the open ones; each is finished, cancelled, or moved on its own (`references/closing.md`, section 7).
   `toolkit work list --tree`
7. Memory: at most one `event` record through `memory-save`, only when the episode will matter later.
8. Before Done, run the Done checklist in `references/approvals.md`, section 5, with the Overview and Roadmap updates and the leftover worktrees in `references/closing.md`, sections 9 and 10. Take the item off the current focus now, before the finish command, so the backup it makes holds the new focus (`references/current-focus.md`); if the finish refuses, put the item back. Then mark it Done. The command also backs up the tracker and memory: read its backup line. "No backup folder is set" or a line with "failed" goes to the owner as a question (`references/closing.md`, section 10).
   `toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>'`
9. Say whether the work reached the default branch. End with the one question (the merge, the deploy, a leftover branch, the backup folder) or "Tell me the next thing to build."
10. Cancel instead: the owner's words are the reason; ask about each open sub-item first (`references/approvals.md`, section 6).
    `toolkit work cancel <id> --reason '<his words>'`

## Gotchas

- Run each `toolkit` command alone: never joined by `&&`, `;`, or a pipe, and never from a script (in Codex that runs it inside the sandbox, where it fails). One-line values go in single quotes, never double quotes; an apostrophe inside them is `'\''` in Claude Code and ’ (U+2019) in Codex, or reword the text. Section text goes on standard input (`--set-file -`) in Claude Code, and in `--text '<text>'` or a `mktemp -d` file in Codex (`references/toolkit-commands.md`, "Text in a command").
- Never mark Done without a recorded result approval or the owner's quoted words. The CLI needs `--by`, and `--quote` when no result approval is recorded.
- Never mark Done while the item's changes, or its `requirements/` and `system-guide/` updates, are uncommitted.
- A result approval never covers merge, deployment, spending, or publishing. Each needs the owner's yes or a standing instruction recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.
- A standing merge instruction needs an `acceptance-checker` that did not build the change to find no blocking issue on that exact head. Without that check, ask the owner.
- Agents never run a production deploy or a production data load. Hand the owner the exact command and what to check afterwards; record his report in a history note.
- In Codex, every Git write needs the owner's approval and escalated permissions (`references/git-rules.md`). No remote: never run `git fetch` or `git push`.
- No AI credit in commits, pull requests, or release notes. The pull request description goes through `unslop`.
- Stages that do not apply are skipped, each with one history note saying so.
- Leave the folder or card where it is. Moving or archiving is `work-organize`'s, on the owner's request.
- GitHub Issues or Jira: `toolkit work` exits with code 3. Close the issue as completed, or as not planned for a cancel (`references/tracker-github.md` or `references/tracker-jira.md`).

## Agents

- `acceptance-checker` (`references/agent-acceptance-checker.md`): the independent check of the exact head before a merge under a standing merge instruction. Brief it as `work-check` does and name the commit (`references/helpers.md`).
- Codex: this plugin's agents do not load there. Give the full text of this skill's `references/agent-<name>.md`, with the brief, to a native Codex worker: the `spawn_agent` tool, started without this conversation (`fork_turns` set to `none`), so a checker never shares the builder's thread. With no worker, do the work yourself and say that no independent check ran. Without an independent check, a standing merge instruction does not apply: ask the owner.

### Active requirements

#### R-01 — `--max` is the one option besides help

**Status:** Finalized  
**Applies to:** Running the slug command with `--max` among its arguments.  
**Required behavior:** `--max` followed by a separate value (`--max 20`) and `--max=` joined to its value (`--max=20`) both set the length limit and are never title text. They may appear anywhere among the arguments; the other words are joined in order as one title, by WI-001 R-04. When `--max` is given more than once, the last one is used and the earlier ones are ignored. `--max` is the only exception to WI-001 R-04: every other argument that starts with `-` is still title text, and `--help` and `-h` show help only when they are the only argument.  
**Boundaries and exceptions:** WI-001 R-04 itself is not changed. Any value R-03 rejects is handled by R-03. The usage and help messages of WI-001 do not mention `--max` (owner, 2026-09-28, Q-05 item 8).  
**Acceptance check:** `node slug.js --max 20 Hello World` prints `hello-world` (the words `--max` and `20` are not in the slug); `node slug.js --max=12 Hello World Again` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js Hello --max 5 World` prints `hello`; `node slug.js --max 5 --max 20 Hello World` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js --max 5 --help` prints `help`; `node slug.js -x` still prints `x`.  
**Decision record:** Owner, 2026-09-28, answer to Q-01: "yes, --max is the one exception to R-04." `--max=20` form, any position, help unchanged, and no mention in usage or help: spec check fixes accepted by the owner in Q-05 ("All yes, except 5: last one wins."). Last one wins: owner, Q-05 item 5. Was: "`--max` and the value that follows it are read as the length limit, never as title text." Approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.  
**Open questions:** None.

#### R-02 — The slug is cut to the limit at a dash

**Status:** Finalized  
**Applies to:** Every run with a valid `--max` value, after the slug is made by WI-001's rules.  
**Required behavior:** The printed slug is at most the `--max` number of characters long. A slug already within the limit is printed unchanged. A longer slug is cut to the longest run of whole words, joined by dashes, that is at most the `--max` number of characters. When the first word alone is longer than the limit, so no whole word fits, that word is cut at exactly the limit.  
**Boundaries and exceptions:** Any value R-03 rejects is handled by R-03.  
**Acceptance check:** `node slug.js --max 20 Hello World` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js --max 12 Hello World Again` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js --max 11 Hello World Again` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js --max 5 Internationalization` prints `inter`.  
**Decision record:** Owner, 2026-09-28: Agreed goal ("cut at a dash so no word is split"), and answer to Q-02: "yes, cut that word at exactly the limit." **Status:** Finalized  
**Applies to:** Running the command with a `--max` value that is missing or is not a whole number greater than 0. **Required behavior:** The command prints `Error: --max needs a whole number greater than 0` on standard error (the error output), prints nothing on standard output, and ends with a failure exit code (1).  
**Boundaries and exceptions:** When `--max` is given more than once, only the last value is checked (R-01).

# Slug command

## Purpose and scope

The slug command turns a title into a URL slug from the command line: `node slug.js "<title>"`. Anyone who runs it from a checkout of this project is a user. The slug docs site and its usage page are not covered here.

## Functional behavior

### SLUG-01 — The command prints the slug of the title

- Trigger or context: Running `node slug.js "<title>"`.
- Required behavior: The command prints the slug of the title, made by SLUG-02 and SLUG-03, on one line on standard output, and ends with exit code 0.
- Conditions and exceptions: No title, or nothing left after the rules: SLUG-04. Several words, help, and `--max`: SLUG-05 to SLUG-07.
- User or system outcome: `node slug.js "Hello World"` prints `hello-world`.
- Source: WI-001 R-01, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 16e745a); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-02 — Slug rules

- Trigger or context: Every title the command turns into a slug.
- Required behavior: (1) All letters become lowercase. (2) Spaces and punctuation become dashes, and a run of several becomes a single dash. (3) Dashes at the start and end are removed. (4) Latin letters with accents or strokes become plain letters: é becomes e, ø becomes o, ł becomes l, đ becomes d, ß becomes ss, æ becomes ae, œ becomes oe.
- Conditions and exceptions: Apostrophes are removed without a dash (SLUG-03).
- User or system outcome: `"  Hello,  World!! "` gives `hello-world`; `"Café Déjà Vu"` gives `cafe-deja-vu`; `"Straße Søren"` gives `strasse-soren`.
- Source: WI-001 R-02, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 16e745a); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-03 — Characters a slug may hold

- Trigger or context: Every title the command turns into a slug.
- Required behavior: A slug holds only the letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9, and single dashes between them. Apostrophes (' and ’) are removed without leaving a dash. Every other character that is not a letter or digit after SLUG-02 rule 4 (for example underscores, emoji, or letters from non-Latin alphabets) is treated like punctuation.
- Conditions and exceptions: A title made only of such characters falls under SLUG-04.
- User or system outcome: `"Don't Stop 2 Believe_Now"` gives `dont-stop-2-believe-now`; `"It’s 🎉 Time"` gives `its-time`.
- Source: WI-001 R-05, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 16e745a); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-04 — Nothing to turn into a slug is an error

- Trigger or context: No title, an empty title, or a title with no letters or digits left after the rules (for example `"!!!"`).
- Required behavior: The command prints `Usage: node slug.js "<title>"` on standard error, nothing on standard output, and ends with exit code 1.
- Conditions and exceptions: With a bad `--max` value, SLUG-07's error is printed instead.
- User or system outcome: `node slug.js`, `node slug.js ""`, and `node slug.js "!!!"` each fail with the usage message.
- Source: WI-001 R-03 and WI-002 R-04, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 2ef81c2); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-05 — Several words without quotes, and help

- Trigger or context: Several arguments, for example `node slug.js Hello World`, or asking for help.
- Required behavior: The words are joined with spaces and treated as one title. When the only argument is `--help` or `-h`, the command prints the usage message on standard output and ends with exit code 0. Any other argument that starts with `-` is title text, except `--max` (SLUG-06).
- Conditions and exceptions: `--help` with any other argument is title text.
- User or system outcome: `node slug.js Hello World` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js -x` prints `x`; `node slug.js --max 5 --help` prints `help`.
- Source: WI-001 R-04 and WI-002 R-01, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 2ef81c2); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-06 — `--max` limits the slug length

- Trigger or context: `--max <n>` or `--max=<n>` anywhere among the arguments.
- Required behavior: `--max` and its value set the length limit and are never title text. When `--max` is given more than once, the last one is used. The printed slug is at most that many characters. A longer slug is cut to the longest run of whole words, joined by dashes, that fits. When the first word alone is longer than the limit, that word is cut at exactly the limit.
- Conditions and exceptions: The usage and help messages do not mention `--max`. A bad value: SLUG-07.
- User or system outcome: `node slug.js --max 12 Hello World Again` prints `hello-world`; `node slug.js --max 5 Internationalization` prints `inter`; `node slug.js --max 5 --max 20 Hello World` prints `hello-world`.
- Source: WI-002 R-01 and R-02, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 2ef81c2); automated tests pass.

### SLUG-07 — A bad `--max` value is an error

- Trigger or context: A `--max` value that is missing or is not made of the digits 0 to 9 alone with a value above 0 (for example nothing, `0`, `abc`, `-3`, `2.5`, `5abc`, `+5`, `1e2`).
- Required behavior: The command prints `Error: --max needs a whole number greater than 0` on standard error, nothing on standard output, and ends with exit code 1.
- Conditions and exceptions: Only the last `--max` value is checked. This error wins over the usage error when there is also no title.
- User or system outcome: `node slug.js --max abc Hello` fails with the error message.
- Source: WI-002 R-03 and R-04, approved by Mike Rihm on 2026-09-28.
- Delivery status and evidence: Delivered on main (commit 2ef81c2); automated tests pass.

## Data and access rules

None. The command reads only its arguments and stores nothing.

## Integrations and dependencies

Node.js, with no other dependencies. CI runs it on Node 22 (owner, 2026-09-28).

## Acceptance evidence

`node --test` from the project root runs `test/slug.test.js`, which covers every example above: 24 pass, 0 fail at commit 2ef81c2 on 2026-09-28. The owner ran the command himself and approved WI-001 and WI-002 on 2026-09-28.

## Change history

- 2026-09-28 — Slug command delivered — WI-001.
- 2026-09-28 — `--max` length limit delivered — WI-002.
